nodes.title: Osric the Lamplighter
nodes.speaker: osric
nodes.text: An old man in an oilskin coat crouches at the crossroads, shielding a Lantern from the rain with his own body. "Forty years I've lit this glass," he mutters, "and tonight it won't take a spark. It's as if something drank the light right out of it." [page] He squints past you at the green glow on the hill. "Whatever that is up there, it's the first light I've seen tonight that isn't afraid of the dark."

nodes.title: Osric the Lamplighter
nodes.speaker: osric
nodes.text: Osric stares at the green glow under your coat, and for a long moment he says nothing. "Whatever you're carrying," he says at last, "hold it up to the glass."

nodes.title: Osric the Lamplighter
nodes.speaker: osric
nodes.text: Osric stares at the flame, then at the lump under your coat. "Green," he says at last. "I'd forgotten it could burn green." [page] He sits down hard on the Lantern's step, as if his legs have only now remembered how old they are. "Ask, then. I can see you've questions. I've had all my life to think up answers."

nodes.title: Osric the Lamplighter
nodes.speaker: osric
nodes.text: "The Lantern's holding," Osric says, warming his hands. "So are you, by the look of it."

choices.label: What has become of the world?

nodes.title: Osric the Lamplighter
nodes.speaker: osric
nodes.text: "Back already?" Osric says without looking up. "The light kept you. It always does... until it doesn't."

nodes.title: Osric the Lamplighter
nodes.speaker: osric
nodes.text: Osric warms his hands at the glass and waits.

choices.label: What has become of the world?

nodes.title: Osric the Lamplighter
nodes.speaker: osric
nodes.text: "When I was a boy, every road in Valdren had a Lantern, and every Lantern burned. Travellers slept beside them and woke whole." [page] "Then the light began to thin. Not all at once. A Lantern would gutter here, go cold there, and the keepers grew old with nobody to follow them." [page] "Where the light goes out, the ash creeps in. You've seen the beasts in the meadow, the way their eyes catch the dark. They weren't like that once." [page] "The Ashen Circle call it the Long Dusk, and they pray for it. I call it a winter that forgot to end."

nodes.title: Osric the Lamplighter
nodes.speaker: osric
nodes.text: "A Lantern remembers whoever rests by it. Sit a while and your hurts close, the draught at your belt fills again, and the creatures you've put down get up and walk the dark once more." [page] "Fall out there and you'll wake beside the last Lantern you rested at. The light keeps you. That's its whole bargain." [page] "It won't keep what you carried, mind. That stays where you fell, glowing, till you fetch it back or fall again first."

nodes.title: Osric the Lamplighter
nodes.speaker: osric
nodes.text: "Every ash-touched thing holds a sliver of the old light, stolen. Strike it down and the sliver goes free, and that stone of yours drinks it." [page] "Spend them here, at the glass. The Lantern turns borrowed light into you: a stronger arm, a steadier breath, a harder skin." [page] "Hoard them and you'll lose them. I've watched braver folk than you learn that twice."

nodes.title: Osric the Lamplighter
nodes.speaker: osric
nodes.text: "West, past the flooded road, lies the Whispering Wood; from the mill you'd reach it south across the ford, once the water falls. The Wardens there don't love strangers, and they love the Circle less." [page] "Under the hills, the Hollow Deep, where the old kings are buried and some of them won't stay so. Beyond it, the city: all banners, all lies." [page] "And past everything, where the ground turns to cinder, a spire of crystal you can see on a clear night. Nobody I know has walked there and come back to say so." [page] He looks at your coat again. "If that stone is what I think it is, every one of those roads will want a look at you."

nodes.title: Osric the Lamplighter
nodes.speaker: osric
nodes.text: "Rest when you can. The dark doesn't."
